transcript:
Meeting Header:
- Date/Time: 2026-08-01 11:00 PT
- Duration: 52 minutes
- Attendees: Marcus (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Owen (Redwood CSM), Samantha (MapleGate Head of ML), Derek (Infra), Priya K (PM), Jordan (Security)

Summary:
- Quick QBR-style checkin focused on stability incidents last month, cost spikes during peak trading windows, and a decision path for pilot -> Dedicated capacity. Customer wants a clear tradeoff matrix: latency SLA, unit cost, and compliance gating. Agreed to run a 48h microbench with production-like traces and exchange security artifacts before next decision meeting.

Topics Covered:
1) Recent incidents and root cause theories (cache stampede, autoscale warmup)
2) Peak-hour cost & throttling behavior
3) Deployment topology options (Hosted API vs Redwood Dedicated vs Private VPC)
4) Security/compliance asks for finance workloads
5) Pilot success criteria and rollout timeline

Action items (discussed in call): see action_items metadata above

Transcript:
[00:00] Marcus (AE): hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll keep this tight, 50 minutes ish. quick roll call?
[00:12] Samantha: hi, Sam here. thanks Marcus.
[00:15] Derek: Derek, infra.
[00:18] Priya K: Priya K, product.
[00:20] Jordan: Jordan, security.
[00:22] Priya (SE): Priya from Redwood. Owen from CSM on my left.
[00:26] Marcus: awesome. to set context — saw the incident window last Friday, and Sam you flagged a p95 spike to 1.1s for the customer-facing flows. want to walk us through what you saw and what success looks like for you in a QBR sense.
[00:42] Samantha: yeah so over a 40 minute window we had p95 jump from 320ms to 1.1s. it correlates with heavier batch of long prompts from our compliance ingestion job, plus several small chat queries. it seemed like batching backpressure kicked in and some warmup latency cascaded. we hit a cost spike too cuz retries retried and we had more tokens.
[01:05] Derek: if I can add — our infra had transient CPU pressure on the orchestrator side; we saw kube evictions around the same time. not sure how much that impacted the Redwood client-side backoff.
[01:20] Priya (SE): ok that helps. two fronts: runtime behavior (kv cache usage + batch shaping) and client retry/backoff. we saw similar in another finance customer where prefix caching prevented duplicate work. question — are you shipping KV cache hints from the client today?
[01:38] Samantha: no, we haven't instrumented prefix hints yet. we're on an older SDK tilt, some of our calls still go through a homegrown gateway that doesn't forward kv cache markers.
[01:54] Marcus: that's a helpful callout. for the pilot decision we should separate infra fixes (your gateway) from serving profile changes (batching/quantization). both affect cost/latency but differently.
[02:10] Priya K: on product side our timeline is tight — we want pilot decision by mid-August so we can schedule rollout for September. main criteria: p95 under 400ms for the user chat route, and total token cost under our current budget (we gave numbers earlier in the shared sheet).
[02:31] Marcus: noted. Owen - any reliability notes?
[02:35] Owen (CSM): yes, last month we had two failover windows where the fallback policy served a slightly smaller model. the client switched to fallback pretty fast which kept availability but raised your per-token cost by about 18% during those minutes. we can show the per-route cost delta post-call.
[02:55] Samantha: can you explain fallback more? is fallback automatic if a model is busy? is it region-based?
[03:03] Priya (SE): fallback is policy-driven. you can pick to fallback by latency threshold, capacity tier, or region; it's usually to a smaller model variant or a different pool. it keeps availability but yes, smaller model often increases token counts due to extra decoding and sometimes costs more in throughput. weird but true for some reheating patterns.
[03:25] Derek: we've also looked at Dedicated pools. curious about commit tiers and how burst works. we need predictable throughput during market opens. spikes are short but intense.
[03:36] Marcus: Dedicated gives reserved GPUs and predictable throughput—autoscale and burst are configurable. tradeoff is you pay for reserved headroom. we can sketch three scenarios: small dedicated for p95 reliability, medium commit for peak windows, or hosted with aggressive cache/batching and traffic shaping.
[03:54] Priya K: when you say hosted with aggressive cache, do you mean prefix caching and re-using kv?
[03:58] Priya (SE): yeah, so two levers: prefix/KV caching on the runtime side and client hints to increase cache hits. on top of that, continuous batching config — you can tune max batch latency vs batch size which directly changes p50/p95. we'll demo config tradeoffs in the bench.
[04:18] Jordan (Security): quick security lens — we need network diagrams, SOC2 attestation, and evidence of KMS integration. also encryption-in-transit and at-rest. anything on Private deployment that simplifies audits?
[04:31] Marcus: Private (our VPC option) offers a customer-controlled network plane and can be set up with KMS/HSM integrates. we have SOC2 docs and an audit pack, will send. note that Private can add 2-3 weeks to setup depending on networking and firewall rules.
[04:50] Jordan: timeline matters. legal will need the docs for their review, and we may need an on-site or deeper pen test if data residency is an issue.
[04:58] Samantha: data residency — all data stays in US for us. we just need to be sure logs don't leak PII to analytics.
[05:05] Owen: we can redact token-level PII on ingestion and keep detailed trace logs only in the customer project space.
[05:12] Marcus: good. on cost modeling, Sam, do you have the average tokens per request and monthly volume handy?
[05:18] Samantha: yep — average 420 tokens/request, peak 1200 req/s for a 3 minute market-open spike, monthly active users around 1.2M though concurrency is the real kicker.
[05:32] Priya (SE): that'll be useful for the bench. Derek, can you share a histogram of sequence lengths and an RPS trace for the last two weeks? that will make our microbench mimic production.
[05:42] Derek: yes, I'll extract and share. expect it by Thursday.
[05:46] Marcus: perfect. now on instrumentation — we noticed some customers had issues because SDK version mismatches caused missing headers for caching. Sam, which SDK are you on?
[05:56] Samantha: still on 0.9.1 from last year. we haven't upgraded to the 1.x line.
[06:02] Priya (SE): ok 0.9.1 misses the kv-cache header and has different streaming semantics. upgrade will reduce duplicate generation and unlock client-side cache hints. we'll include an upgrade guide in the post-call notes.
[06:17] Samantha: how risky is upgrade in prod?
[06:19] Priya (SE): low — we can run canary traffic, and the client is backwards-compatible in most paths, but we recommend a short canary with synthetic traffic.
[06:30] Marcus: decision framework time — we sketched three options: A) short-term Hosted with SDK upgrade + caching + client changes; B) Dedicated pilot with a small commit that covers peak; C) Private VPC for full audit and isolation. Sam, which aligns with your procurement preference?
[06:48] Samantha: procurement likes predictable costs, but legal pushes back on setup delay for Private. product wants speed. i'd prefer B if we can get a clear ROI comparison and the dedicated pricing doesn't overshoot our budget.
[07:01] Derek: agree with B leaning. but we need burst behavior — if a dedicated pool is saturated, what's the fallback?
[07:09] Priya (SE): you can configure cross-pool fallback to hosted as a graceful overflow; you'll pay hosted rates for overflow but keep availability. we can add an autoscale buffer and configure priority traffic to avoid overflow for critical routes.
[07:26] Jordan: if overflow goes to hosted, what about logs, audit trails—will you centralize them in our account?
[07:33] Marcus: we can centralize logs in your project and keep audit trails; when overflow hits hosted, the request metadata still tags your account id. we'll include the logging sequence in the network diagram pack.
[07:46] Samantha: ok great. can you put together a simple cost delta: hosted vs dedicated with overflow scenario? i want to show finance two numbers not three.
[07:55] Marcus: yes — Marcus will do a sketch.
[07:58] Owen: for the 48h bench we plan three phases: mimic steady-state traffic, a market-open spike, and a recovery window. we'll capture p50/p95, cold-starts, and model quality diffs if we change variants.
[08:13] Priya K: about quality diffs — can you guarantee same model outputs if fallback occurs? some of our business logic depends on deterministic ranking.
[08:21] Priya (SE): different model variants will have small distributional changes. we recommend an eval prompt set to detect regressions. Redwood Optimize can run continuous drift checks tied to your prompt suite. we'll run a small eval during the bench.
[08:36] Samantha: that helps. also curious about quantization — do you recommend int8 for our finance prompts?
[08:42] Priya (SE): depends. int8 can reduce cost but might slightly change output probabilities. for business-critical scoring we recommend mixed strategy: int8 for non-critical routes, fp16 or calibrated quant for ranking. we'll include quantization recommendation after bench.
[08:58] Derek: any gotchas on GPU family selection for Dedicated? A100 vs H100 differences?
[09:05] Marcus: H100s higher throughput but different kernel path; A100 is well-tuned for certain models and sequences. for shorter seq lengths you might be better on H100 for throughput at lower latency if kernels line up. we'll put a recommended mapping after we see your seq histogram.
[09:23] Jordan: timeline recap?
[09:25] Marcus: ok recapping — SE will run 48h microbench using Derek traces (due 2026-08-04); Marcus will send pricing scenarios for Dedicated/Hosted with overflow math (due 2026-08-06); Jordan gets SOC2 and network diagram (we'll send by 2026-08-03); follow-up decision meeting targeted 2026-08-10 to confirm pilot path.
[09:45] Samantha: perfect. one more Q on throttling — we saw 429 spikes even when capacity looked available, any hints?
[09:51] Priya (SE): likely client-side throttles or gateway rate limits; also some infra throttling when autoscale was spinning up. add low-latency warming and tune client-side concurrency to avoid sudden bursts.
[10:06] Derek: we'll tune the gateway and add a short tokenized queue.
[10:09] Marcus: great. any blockers from legal/security?
[10:12] Jordan: send docs and we'll triage. request a short threat model doc for finance-specific concerns.
[10:20] Marcus: will do. any other questions?
[10:23] Samantha: no, thanks everyone.
[10:25] Marcus: thanks all — Owen will follow up with notes. meeting end.

Post-meeting notes (brief):
- Bench plan attached: 3-phase microbench to reproduce steady, spike, recovery.
- Priority: get SDK upgrade in canary, share sequence histograms, send SOC2 + network diagram.
- Intended decision: pick Dedicated pilot if bench shows p95 <= 400ms with acceptable cost delta; otherwise iterate on hosted optimizations.

Links mentioned / artifacts to be shared:
- bench-spreadsheet (link): https://redwood-internal.example/bench/mgf-2026-48h (placeholder)
- SOC2 pack and network diagram: will be uploaded to shared drive
- pricing sketch: will be attached to CRM

Meeting closed at ~11:52 PT
